variants.asks: and the same narrowings counted in the points that stand at a local - the point and everything folded into it. What do the rules do to the space at a local?
variants.leads: THE SPACE AT A LOCAL: half a point for every meeting seen from l's end, since a meeting folds one of its two points into the other, and one point handed back by every creation.

parts.because: the facing factor is (1 - d^·j^)/2 and j^ is what the opposing population is doing on average. Alike in every direction, that is nothing - so a meeting in an undisturbed vacuum carries exactly a half, and the two limits it interpolates are one head-on and nought co-moving

parts.is: the space count of what is taken
parts.because: READ OFF THE CONTINUOUS MODEL - the term - \sigma Fn\tilde{n} of the continuous model: -2 rays a firing, at rate \sigma, on the share F of the matches, of degree 2 in the density; what this fact takes from it is below. ANNIHILATION fires at \sigma·F·\rho^{2}, and ONE firing of it puts -1 into the space ledger - counted off the body, not written down. The two ledgers get different counts from the same firing, which is why they do not settle at the same density

steps.because: the rules, read as a line: every rule of the theory is a term, the reading having run each rule's program on a symbolic match and counted what it does to the population - what it makes, what it takes, what it carries, what a body puts in - so the line is what the rules come to as a crowd rather than a description of them. Everything a theorem of this theory stands on is a term of this line or a reading of one, so every premise below is read off it, and every derivation passes through it

steps.via: the space at a local, as the rules narrow it
steps.because: the same narrowings, counted in the points that stand at l. A meeting folds one of its two ends into the other, so l, seen from one end, gains half a point a meeting; and a creation hands one point back, whatever l holds - a firing is one event on one point. What the world grows behind a meeting or ahead of a ray is a new local, not a point standing here.

derivation.via: an edge, seen from one of its ends
working: Edge.active = this.initial != None & this.terminal != None & this.initial.active & this.terminal.active
Ray.facing = this.terminal.across.ray: the ray across the same edge - next
derivation.because: an edge is active by its own definition: every end it joins is active. Seen from l, one of those ends is l's own ray and the others are across the edge from it - the ray `facing` reads, which is l's ray's next one. So a meeting is a ray of l that is lit and whose next ray is lit, and one meeting is as many of l's members as the definition has ends: 2.

working: Vertex.sinks = this.folded_into == None ? Vector.zero(this.at.components.length) : this.folded_into.at - this.at
derivation.because: the points that stand at l: l itself, and every point folded into it - `held`, each with `folded_into` set to l. A folded point is not alive and it sinks into the point that holds it, so its place is l's, and @ == l is the one narrowing for both. The space a firing moves at a local is this count, a swallow one more and a hand-back one fewer; what the world grows is a new local, not a point standing here.

the rule fires on an edge: its pattern, as a narrowing of l, is \narrow{l}{active & next.active}. One firing moves 1 on the space, and one match is 2 of l's members, so each member of the narrowing moves \frac{1}{2}.
the rule fires on a point: its pattern, as a narrowing of l, is \narrow{l}{neutral}. One firing moves -1 on the space, and one match is 1 of l's members, so each member of the narrowing moves -1.
